explain.say: When your earbuds play music from your phone, you are using a network! A network is just two or more devices joined so they can share things. Networks come in sizes, like boxes inside boxes. Look at the board: the biggest of all, the internet.

explain.say: Now zoom to a LAN, a local area network: the computers in one school, office or home. Look at the board: here is a school LAN. Each computer plugs into a switch, the switch links to the router, and the router links to the internet. Can you follow a cable from the printer to the internet?
The smallest is a PAN, a personal area network, like a smartwatch or earbuds talking to your phone by Bluetooth. Look at the last level. How many PANs are you wearing right now?

faq.a: A LAN, local area network, connects devices in one small area like a home, school or office, using cables or Wi-Fi.
asks: Is my home Wi-Fi a LAN?

faq.a: A WAN, wide area network, connects networks that are far apart, across cities or countries, often using leased lines. The internet is the biggest WAN.
asks: What is the difference between a LAN and a WAN?

faq.a: A switch is a box that connects computers on a LAN and sends each message only to the device it is meant for.
asks: What does a network switch do?

faq.a: A router connects different networks, such as your home LAN and the internet, and sends each packet towards the right network.
asks: How does my router connect me to the internet?

faq.a: Yes, it is a network of networks: millions of home, school, company and phone networks all connected by routers and cables around the world.
asks: What is the internet made of?
Why is the internet called a network of networks?

facts: Bluetooth is named after Harald Bluetooth, a 10th-century king who united parts of Denmark and Norway.
LAN stands for local area network and WAN for wide area network.
